name: Constituent Services
description:
This dataset records constituent service requests handled by a city government, with each row representing a case tied to a contact, a council member, a community board, and a location. It includes 1,274 sampled rows and 13 columns covering contact and case identifiers, city, state, postal code, council member name and district number, community board number, case type and subtype, case subject, start and end dates, and case status.

Most records are located in New York (NY), with postal codes concentrated in Manhattan-area ranges. Housing is the most common case type (about 40%), followed by NYCHA (about 23%) and Other (about 12%). Case subjects include issues such as rent arrears, repairs, security deposits, and quality of life concerns. About 65% of cases are marked Closed and 34% Pending, with a small number flagged Urgent. End dates are missing for roughly two-thirds of cases, reflecting unresolved or still-open requests.

Semantic summary (topic and possible uses):
This dataset contains records of constituent service requests handled by a city government, tracking individual cases from intake through resolution. Each row links a contact to a council member, community board, and location, along with case details such as type, subject, start and end dates, and current status. It belongs to the municipal government and civic administration domain, likely supporting case management and constituent relations work. Possible uses include analyzing request volumes and response times by district or case type, identifying service trends and recurring neighborhood issues, evaluating council member and community board workloads, and building dashboards or reports to improve government responsiveness and resource allocation.
